hero.headline: Trump replaces intelligence director with housing official
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard following her recent departure from the role.

Gabbard announced her resignation in a letter to the president, stating she would leave her position on June 30. She cited her husband's recent diagnosis with a rare form of bone cancer as the reason for stepping down from public service. A spokesperson for Gabbard's office denied reports that she had been forced out, calling such claims "100% false." However, Reuters reported that the White House had pressured her to resign, citing sources familiar with the matter.

Trump issued a statement on his Truth Social platform saying Gabbard "has done an incredible job, and we will miss her." He indicated that Aaron Lukas, principal deputy director of national intelligence, would initially serve as acting director before announcing Pulte's appointment days later.

Gabbard's tenure had been marked by significant challenges. Despite her efforts to align herself with Trump's agenda, including pledges to root out politicization in intelligence agencies and her embrace of election denial claims, she became increasingly sidelined by the president. Trump excluded her from key national security discussions regarding Iran and Venezuela, according to people familiar with her office. She was an unconventional choice for the role from the start, lacking an intelligence background and bringing foreign policy views that sometimes diverged from Trump's positions on military intervention abroad.

Pulte's appointment to lead the nation's intelligence apparatus represents an unusual selection for a position that typically requires extensive national security or intelligence experience. As an heir to a home construction company fortune, Pulte brings no background in intelligence or national security matters to the role.

The selection has drawn immediate criticism. Senate Majority Leader John Thune stated that the country does not need a weaponized director of national intelligence. Reports indicate that Pulte has previously demonstrated a willingness to pursue individuals perceived as enemies by the president.

The director of national intelligence serves as the principal advisor to the president on intelligence matters and oversees coordination among 18 intelligence organizations, including the CIA and NSA. The position was created after the September 11 attacks to improve information sharing among agencies. The acting designation means Pulte will serve without Senate confirmation, at least temporarily.

The intelligence community has faced ongoing scrutiny regarding its independence from political influence, with concerns from both parties about whether assessments are shaped by objective analysis or partisan considerations.

cards.headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv After Weeklong Threat Campaign, Killing 22
cards.body:
Russian forces launched a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv early Sunday morning, killing at least 22 people and wounding 20 others. The strikes hit multiple residential buildings across several districts of the capital, forcing emergency workers to conduct extensive search and rescue operations.

The attack came shortly after Ukraine's air force warned that Russia might deploy its Oreshnik hypersonic ballistic missile. Explosions echoed through the city after 1 a.m., affecting at least four locations in the Shevchenkivsky, Dniprovsky, and Podilsky districts. Fire broke out on the premises of a school in the city center, and debris damaged multiple residential structures across Kyiv.

The timing reflects Moscow's strategic approach of combining psychological pressure with physical assault. Russian officials had announced the potential strike days in advance, a method designed to amplify anxiety in the Ukrainian capital before the missiles arrived. This strategy appears aimed at compensating for recent battlefield setbacks by intensifying attacks on civilian areas.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia's use of the Oreshnik missile "sets a global precedent for other potential aggressors." He called on the international community to apply preventive pressure on Moscow rather than responding only after attacks occur. "If Russia is allowed to destroy lives on such a scale, then no agreement will restrain other similar hatred-based regimes from aggression and strikes," Zelenskyy said.

The Oreshnik missile, which Putin has claimed is impossible to intercept due to its reported speed exceeding 10 times the sound barrier, has now been deployed twice against Ukraine. Russia has also positioned the weapon in Belarus, which borders Ukraine and three NATO member states.

Canada strongly condemned the attack, with Prime Minister Mark Carney urging Moscow to cease its "illegal war of aggression." He stated that such strikes "prolong human suffering and do nothing to change the fact that Russia will lose this war."

The strike follows escalating tensions along the conflict lines. Russia claimed that Ukrainian forces had struck a student dormitory in Starobilsk in occupied Lugansk, resulting in 18 deaths. Ukraine denied targeting civilians, insisting it had struck a Russian drone unit stationed in the area.

The attack on Kyiv underscores the conflict's evolving nature as Russia faces mounting military pressures. Moscow's shift toward intensified strikes on population centers suggests the leadership believes demonstrating destructive capability may offset territorial losses and provide leverage in potential future negotiations. The human toll continues to mount on both sides as the conflict persists.

cards.headline: Iran withdraws from ceasefire talks as Lebanon fighting continues
cards.teaser: Iran stopped communicating with mediators following renewed conflict between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran has halted talks with U.S. mediators over Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza, according to Iranian reports. The breakdown in negotiations comes as clashes between Israel and Hezbollah continue despite both sides accepting a U.S. partial ceasefire plan.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared before Congress as the ceasefire efforts faltered. President Trump stated that negotiations with Iran remain active, while indicating that Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting once Iran resumes talks with the U.S.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon Despite Pulling Back From Beirut Threat
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu backed away from attacking Beirut under pressure from President Trump but vowed to continue operations against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel continued strikes on southern Lebanon on Tuesday after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu decided against attacking Beirut following pressure from President Trump. According to reports, Trump angrily confronted Netanyahu over the threat to resume airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs during a Monday phone call.

Netanyahu stated Israel would maintain its campaign against Hezbollah despite backing away from striking the Lebanese capital. Both Israel and Hezbollah have accepted a US partial ceasefire plan, though clashes continue in Lebanon. A cessation of hostilities between the two groups is viewed as crucial to broader peace negotiations with Iran, which suspended talks with the US over Israel's Lebanon campaign.

cards.headline: Iran Announces Three-Day Funeral for Ayatollah Khamenei
cards.teaser: Ceremonies for the deceased Iranian leader will take place across multiple cities, with Tehran expected to draw up to 20 million attendees.
cards.body:
Iran has announced a three-day funeral plan for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, following what state media described as a long delay. Ceremonies will be held in multiple cities across the country, according to Iranian state media reports.

Authorities in Tehran expect up to 20 million people to attend the funeral events in the capital. The announcement comes after an extended period during which funeral plans had not been disclosed, though the reasons for the delay were not specified in the state media coverage.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazil Over Trade Practices
cards.teaser: The administration initiated a Section 301 investigation targeting Brazil, citing concerns about unfair trade practices.
cards.body:
The Trump administration proposed a 25 percent tariff on Brazilian imports, marking the latest expansion of its trade enforcement strategy. Officials cited unfair trade practices as the basis for the tariff proposal, which was announced through a Section 301 investigation.

The move represents the administration's continued efforts to reshape trade policy through investigative mechanisms that allow for unilateral tariff actions. Section 301 investigations grant the executive branch authority to impose duties on imports when unfair trade practices are identified. Brazil becomes the newest target in a broader strategy to address what officials characterize as imbalanced trade relationships.

cards.headline: Canada Requests Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc formally asked the U.S. and Mexico to renew the USMCA agreement.
cards.body:
Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has formally requested the renewal of the USMCA trade agreement in a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico. The request launches the official process for extending the trade deal beyond its current term.

The USMCA replaced NAFTA and establishes the framework governing trade relationships between the three North American nations.

cards.headline: U.S. Ebola Quarantine Plan in Kenya Faces New Court Delay
cards.teaser: A court ruling further postponed the Trump administration's proposal for a quarantine unit for Americans exposed to Ebola, a plan that has sparked protests.
cards.body:
A court in Kenya issued a ruling that further delayed the Trump administration's proposed quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola. The plan has sparked angry protests in Kenya, with demonstrations occurring near the proposed treatment site.

The facility would house U.S. citizens who have been exposed to the virus and require isolation. The court decision represents another setback for the administration's efforts to establish the quarantine unit in the country.

cards.headline: South Africa Investigates Killing of Two Mozambican Men
cards.teaser: Police opened an investigation after two deaths in Mossel Bay following violent protests against illegal migration.
cards.body:
South African police are investigating the deaths of two Mozambican men in Mossel Bay following anti-migrant violence in the area. The killings mark the first deaths officially linked to a wave of anti-immigration protests sweeping the country.

Mozambique has reported that five of its nationals were killed in what it describes as xenophobic attacks in South Africa over the weekend, and the government is working to repatriate hundreds of its citizens from the country.

cards.headline: British Couple Loses Appeal Against Iran Jail Sentence
cards.teaser: Lindsay and Craig Foreman remain imprisoned in Iran after being arrested during a global motorbike journey.
cards.body:
A British couple imprisoned in Iran lost their appeal against their jail sentences, according to family members. Lindsay and Craig Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while traveling through Iran during a global motorbike journey.

The couple's family confirmed the unsuccessful appeal. The original sentences and charges against the Foremans were not specified in available information, though they have now been detained for over a year.

cards.headline: Canada Requests Renewal of North American Trade Pact
cards.teaser: Canadian Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc formally asked the U.S. and Mexico to renew the USMCA agreement.
cards.body:
Canada's Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has formally requested the renewal of the USMCA trade agreement in a letter to his counterparts in the United States and Mexico. The request launches the official process for extending the trade deal beyond its current term.

The USMCA replaced NAFTA and establishes the framework governing trade relationships between the three North American nations.

cards.headline: Doctors examined Biden immediately after debate over stroke concerns
cards.teaser: Medical staff checked the president in the moments following the Trump debate, not days later as the administration previously stated.
cards.body:
Medical personnel examined President Biden immediately after his debate with Donald Trump, according to revelations in former First Lady Jill Biden's new book. Jill Biden feared her husband had suffered a stroke during or after the debate.

This timeline contradicts earlier statements from the Biden administration, which said doctors examined the president days following the debate rather than in the moments after. The former first lady disclosed these details in her recently published memoir.

cards.headline: California holds primary for governor as Newsom term ends
cards.teaser: Voters cast ballots in several states, with the race to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom going down to the wire.
cards.body:
Californians voted in a primary election to choose candidates who will compete to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom. The gubernatorial race remained close as voters went to the polls, capping a primary campaign described as turbulent. Statewide races and congressional district contests also appeared on ballots.

Early voting turnout in some counties, including El Dorado County, ran lower than in previous elections. The primary determines which candidates will advance to the general election for governor and other offices. Newsom is term-limited and cannot seek another term as governor.

cards.headline: Iran withdraws from ceasefire talks as Lebanon fighting continues
cards.teaser: Iran stopped communicating with mediators following renewed conflict between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.
cards.body:
Iran has halted talks with U.S. mediators over Israeli military operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza, according to Iranian reports. The breakdown in negotiations comes as clashes between Israel and Hezbollah continue despite both sides accepting a U.S. partial ceasefire plan.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared before Congress as the ceasefire efforts faltered. President Trump stated that negotiations with Iran remain active, while indicating that Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting once Iran resumes talks with the U.S.

cards.headline: Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 22 people including child
cards.teaser: An eight-year-old boy died in an attack on an apartment building as rescue workers pulled bodies from rubble.
cards.body:
Russia launched 73 missiles and 656 drones across Ukraine overnight, targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Poltava and Kharkiv. The barrage killed at least 22 people and injured dozens more, with some trapped beneath collapsed apartment buildings.

An eight-year-old boy was among those killed when a residential building was struck. Rescue workers recovered bodies from the rubble of damaged structures as emergency operations continued across multiple Ukrainian cities hit in the coordinated attack.

cards.headline: British couple loses appeal of Iran prison sentences
cards.teaser: Lindsay and Craig Foreman were arrested during a global motorcycle journey and had their jail sentences upheld.
cards.body:
A British couple lost their appeal of prison sentences handed down by Iranian courts, according to their family. Lindsay and Craig Foreman were arrested in January 2025 while traveling through Iran during a global motorcycle journey.

The couple had challenged their convictions and sentences through the Iranian legal system. Iranian authorities have not released details about the charges or the length of the sentences. The Foremans' family confirmed the unsuccessful appeal outcome.

cards.headline: Former party executive admits embezzling funds using fake invoices
cards.teaser: Peter Murrell used fabricated invoices to cover up spending of 400,000 pounds from party accounts.
cards.body:
Peter Murrell, former chief executive of the Scottish National Party, has admitted to embezzling £400,000 from the party by using fake invoices to conceal his spending. He pleaded guilty to the embezzlement charges.

Murrell now faces a lengthy prison sentence following his admission. The guilty plea brought the criminal case examining his financial activities while leading the party to a close.

hero.headline: Job Openings Reach Highest Level in Nearly Two Years
hero.body:
Job openings in the United States climbed to 7.6 million in April, marking the highest level in nearly two years, according to new federal data. The increase comes despite economic uncertainty stemming from the ongoing conflict with Iran and represents a significant indicator of labor market strength.

The jump in available positions signals continued employer demand for workers across multiple sectors. Professional services led the growth in job openings, demonstrating resilience in white-collar employment even as broader economic conditions remain uncertain. The data also showed a decline in layoffs during the same period, suggesting companies are maintaining their workforces and continuing to seek new employees.

The robust job openings figures stand in contrast to concerns about economic disruption from international conflicts. Economists had anticipated potential softening in the labor market as businesses assessed risks related to the Iran war and its effects on global trade and energy prices. Instead, the data indicates employers are moving forward with hiring plans and expansion efforts.

The labor market has proven more durable than many forecasters expected earlier this year. Strong job openings typically correlate with worker leverage in wage negotiations and can contribute to sustained consumer spending, which drives much of the American economy. The current level of openings suggests competition for talent remains intense across industries.

The April figures provide the Federal Reserve with additional information as it weighs monetary policy decisions. A tight labor market with elevated job openings could influence discussions about interest rates and inflation management. The data will likely factor into upcoming economic policy debates as officials balance growth objectives against price stability concerns.

cards.headline: Administration Proposes Blocking Grants That Do Not Support Trump Agenda
cards.teaser: A new proposal would allow federal officials to deny grant funding to organizations that do not align with administration priorities.
cards.body:
The administration has introduced a proposal that would permit officials to block grant funding to organizations deemed unsupportive of President Trump's agenda or those accused of promoting what officials call anti-American values. The measure would give the federal government expanded authority over discretionary funding decisions.

The proposal represents a significant shift in how federal grants are awarded, potentially affecting nonprofits, educational institutions, and other organizations that receive government funding. The criteria for determining alignment with administration priorities and the definition of anti-American values have not been detailed in available information about the proposal.

cards.headline: Trump Donor Transfers $5.5 Million Estate to Kennedy's Anti-Vaccine Group
cards.teaser: A Mellon family heir gave Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s Children's Health Defense about 300 acres of Connecticut property at no cost.
cards.body:
A member of the Mellon family, a major Trump donor, gave roughly 300 acres of adjacent Connecticut properties to Children's Health Defense last year. The estate was valued at $5.5 million and transferred at no cost to the organization.

Children's Health Defense, founded by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has promoted claims questioning vaccine safety and efficacy. The donation represents one of the largest property gifts to an organization focused on vaccine skepticism.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazil Over Trade Practices
cards.teaser: The administration initiated a Section 301 investigation targeting Brazil, citing concerns about unfair trade practices.
cards.body:
The Trump administration proposed a 25 percent tariff on Brazilian imports, marking the latest expansion of its trade enforcement strategy. Officials cited unfair trade practices as the basis for the tariff proposal, which was announced through a Section 301 investigation.

The move represents the administration's continued efforts to reshape trade policy through investigative mechanisms that allow for unilateral tariff actions. Section 301 investigations grant the executive branch authority to impose duties on imports when unfair trade practices are identified. Brazil becomes the newest target in a broader strategy to address what officials characterize as imbalanced trade relationships.

cards.headline: Barry Diller's Company Makes Offer to Acquire MGM Resorts
cards.teaser: Media executive Barry Diller's People Inc. submitted an acquisition proposal for the casino and hospitality company.
cards.body:
Media mogul Barry Diller's People Inc. has proposed acquiring MGM Resorts International for over $18 billion. The offer represents a significant diversification for Diller's digital media company, which has previously focused on internet and media businesses.

The proposal comes weeks after Diller told shareholders that People would deepen its focus on its existing MGM stake, describing the casino operator's stock as "wildly undervalued." The acquisition would bring MGM's Las Vegas Strip properties and other casino operations under Diller's corporate control.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Sales Growth Drives Stock Surge
cards.teaser: The lingerie retailer reported strong bra sales and raised its annual outlook, sending shares up sharply.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret delivered strong first-quarter results, with bra sales fueling growth across the company. The performance exceeded both earnings and revenue expectations, prompting management to raise its full-year outlook. Shares jumped 50 percent following the announcement.

The results reflect progress in Victoria's Secret's brand revitalization efforts. Strong bra sales, a cornerstone category for the retailer, drove the quarter's momentum and signaled confidence that sales strength would persist throughout the year.

cards.headline: Alphabet Plans $80 Billion Stock Sale to Fund AI Expansion
cards.teaser: Google's parent company announced a massive capital raise to finance its artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.
cards.body:
Alphabet has announced plans to raise up to $80 billion in equity to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure investments, marking the largest equity fundraising ever according to analysts. The capital raise includes a $10 billion share purchase by Berkshire Hathaway, the investment group formerly led by Warren Buffett.

The announcement has prompted questions about the economics of the AI boom. Alphabet's shares declined following the news of the stock sale.

hero.headline: Hackers breach Dashlane password manager, steal customer vaults
hero.body:
Dashlane, a prominent password management service, disclosed that attackers gained unauthorized access to customer accounts and obtained encrypted password vaults. The company revealed that hackers used brute-force techniques to circumvent its two-factor authentication system, enabling them to bypass a critical security layer meant to protect accounts when passwords are compromised.

Password managers maintain encrypted copies of user passwords, credit card numbers, and other confidential data. Although these vaults are encrypted and require a master password to unlock, security researchers have cautioned that stolen vaults could potentially be cracked offline if users selected weak master passwords.

The company has not specified the number of affected customers or disclosed when the breach took place. The incident highlights ongoing concerns about the effectiveness of two-factor authentication as a defense mechanism against unauthorized access. Brute-force attacks work by systematically attempting many password or security code combinations in rapid succession until one succeeds. The specific method the attackers employed to defeat Dashlane's two-factor system remains unexplained.

Dashlane is not alone in experiencing security issues. The company joins a growing roster of password managers that have encountered breaches or security incidents in recent years. This comes at a time when millions of people depend on such services to handle dozens or hundreds of online accounts.

Security researchers continue to recommend password managers as a safer option than reusing the same password across multiple websites. However, experts advise users to activate every available security feature and select strong master passwords to minimize risk. They emphasize that while password manager breaches are concerning, the alternative of password reuse presents even greater dangers.

Dashlane has not yet announced plans to contact affected customers directly or described what measures it will implement to prevent future attacks. When password manager breaches occur, users typically need to change their master passwords and examine their stored credentials for any evidence of misuse.

The breach raises significant questions about password manager security at a time when these services have become essential tools for managing digital life. While the companies that provide them generally maintain strong security practices, incidents like this demonstrate that even services specifically designed to protect sensitive information remain vulnerable to sophisticated attacks.

Users who maintain accounts with Dashlane may want to take precautions by changing their master passwords and monitoring their online accounts for suspicious activity. Security experts recommend that anyone using a password manager ensure their master password is both lengthy and complex, combining uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters to resist brute-force attempts.

cards.headline: Anthropic expands AI security tool to critical infrastructure in 15 countries
cards.teaser: The AI company is scaling its Mythos vulnerability detection system to 150 organizations managing power, water, healthcare, and communications systems.
cards.body:
Anthropic is expanding Project Glasswing, its cybersecurity program, to 150 organizations across 15 countries. The initiative focuses on critical infrastructure sectors including power grids, water systems, healthcare facilities, and communications networks—areas where cyberattacks could impact millions of people.

The expansion grants participating organizations access to Claude Mythos, Anthropic's AI system designed to identify security vulnerabilities. The program enables infrastructure operators to detect and address weaknesses before they can be exploited.

cards.headline: Apple ships 1.1 million MacBook Neo units in opening weeks
cards.teaser: The new laptop model marks Apple's push into the mainstream market, according to industry estimates.
cards.body:
Rewrite

Apple's MacBook Neo achieved 1.1 million unit shipments during its initial weeks on the market, according to IDC estimates. The strong early sales indicate the laptop is resonating with buyers outside Apple's core customer base as the company expands into the mainstream market.

The performance suggests Apple's strategy to compete more broadly in the laptop segment is gaining traction with consumers seeking alternatives in the category.

cards.headline: Board raises $20 million for in-person gaming device
cards.teaser: The startup from Mirror founder Brynn Putnam has sold thousands of units of its device designed to bring people together in the same room.
cards.body:
Board, a startup founded by Brynn Putnam, has closed a $20 million Series A funding round led by Union Square Ventures. Putnam previously founded Mirror, the fitness company that sold interactive workout displays.

The company builds what it calls "together tech," gaming devices designed to facilitate in-person social interaction. Board has already sold thousands of units. The startup's approach focuses on physical products that encourage face-to-face engagement rather than remote digital interaction.

cards.headline: UN warns new El Niño phase could begin within weeks
cards.teaser: The natural weather pattern could boost temperatures on a planet already experiencing climate change effects.
cards.body:
A new El Niño weather pattern could emerge within weeks, according to the United Nations. This natural phenomenon is expected to raise global temperatures on a planet already affected by climate change.

El Niño occurs when warm water spreads across the equatorial Pacific Ocean, influencing weather patterns worldwide. The UN warns this emerging phase could rank among the strongest in decades.

cards.headline: Meta tests episodic video feature for Instagram and Facebook Reels
cards.teaser: The company is exploring monetization options for the new Series feature that organizes short videos into episodes.
cards.body:
Meta is testing a new feature called Series that enables creators to organize Reels into episodic collections on Instagram and Facebook. The tool groups related short videos together, mirroring how traditional television structures content into seasons and episodes.

The company is exploring monetization options for Series but has not revealed specific details about potential revenue models. The feature underscores Meta's push to retain both creators and audiences as competition for engagement intensifies across social platforms.

cards.headline: X launches video reaction feature for posts
cards.teaser: The platform now allows users to respond to posts with video recordings.
cards.body:
X introduced a feature that lets users respond to posts with video recordings. The React with Video tool adds another option for engagement beyond text replies, likes, and reposts.

The feature appears designed to encourage creators to produce more content on the platform. Video responses could increase time users spend on X by prompting them to watch reaction clips in addition to original posts.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame basketball coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
hero.body:
Rick Adelman, the Hall of Fame basketball coach who won more than 1,000 games during a nearly 30-year career in the NBA, has died at age 79.

Adelman ranks among the most successful coaches in NBA history, finishing his career with 1,042 wins across stints with the Portland Trail Blazers, Golden State Warriors, Sacramento Kings, Houston Rockets, and Minnesota Timberwolves. His win total places him eighth on the NBA's all-time coaching victories list. He coached from 1988 to 2014, leading teams to the playoffs in 16 of his 23 seasons at the helm.

Known for his offensive creativity and ability to maximize player talent, Adelman guided the Trail Blazers to two NBA Finals appearances in 1990 and 1992. He later transformed the Sacramento Kings into one of the most exciting teams of the early 2000s, leading them to the Western Conference Finals in 2002. His teams were characterized by fluid ball movement and high-scoring offenses that emphasized teamwork over individual dominance.

Adelman was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2021, a recognition that came seven years after his retirement from coaching. Despite never winning an NBA championship, his sustained excellence and influence on modern offensive basketball earned him widespread respect throughout the sport. He was named NBA Coach of the Year in 1989 during his second season with Portland.

Adelman's coaching philosophy influenced a generation of coaches and players who valued team-oriented play. His legacy extends beyond his win total to the style of basketball he championed, which emphasized passing, spacing, and player movement principles that remain central to the modern game.

Throughout his career, Adelman demonstrated an ability to succeed with different rosters and organizations. Whether working with established stars or rebuilding teams, he consistently produced winning basketball. His approach to the game prioritized unselfish play and efficient offensive execution, principles that shaped how teams approach basketball strategy today.

The basketball community widely recognized Adelman's contributions to the sport. His influence could be seen in how subsequent coaches and teams adopted similar offensive philosophies, focusing on ball movement and creating scoring opportunities through spacing and player positioning rather than isolation plays.

Adelman's death marks the loss of one of basketball's most influential figures. His Hall of Fame career and the enduring impact of his coaching methods ensure his place among the sport's all-time greats. The principles he established and promoted continue to shape how basketball is played at the highest levels of professional competition.

cards.headline: Eagles trade wide receiver A.J. Brown to Patriots
cards.teaser: Philadelphia sends the star receiver to New England for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round selection.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have traded star wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, ending months of speculation about his future. In exchange, the Eagles will receive a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027.

Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, had grown frustrated during his time in Philadelphia. The move reunites him with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel as both teams reshape their rosters heading into the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Browns GM says Jared Verse inclusion made Myles Garrett trade possible
cards.teaser: Andrew Berry told reporters he did not seriously consider trading the star pass rusher until Los Angeles included the defensive player in the package.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in exchange for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection who set an NFL single-season sacks record with 23 in 2025.

Browns general manager Andrew Berry said he would not have seriously considered the trade without Verse's inclusion. The linebacker proved to be the decisive factor that convinced Cleveland's front office to move forward with trading one of the league's premier defensive players.

cards.headline: Stephen Curry signs 10-year deal with Li-Ning
cards.teaser: The Golden State Warriors star has ended his sneaker free agency with a contract with the Chinese footwear company.
cards.body:
Stephen Curry has signed a 10-year endorsement contract with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning. The deal concludes Curry's period of sneaker free agency following his exit from Under Armour.

The partnership marks a major move in basketball footwear, establishing Li-Ning as the home of one of the sport's biggest stars. The lengthy 10-year commitment signals the company's significant investment in expanding its basketball presence through Curry's signature line.

cards.headline: Aspiration co-founder Joseph Sanberg sentenced to 14 years in prison
cards.teaser: The green banking company executive received federal prison time in a case connected to an NBA investigation into the Clippers.
cards.body:
Joseph Sanberg, co-founder of the now-bankrupt green banking company Aspiration, was sentenced to 14 years in federal prison on Monday. His company has become the focus of an NBA investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers organization.

The sentencing was handed down in federal court as Aspiration continues through bankruptcy proceedings.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark and Stephanie White deny rift after on-court exchange
cards.teaser: The Indiana Fever star and head coach addressed questions about their relationship following an animated discussion during Saturday's loss.
cards.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark and coach Stephanie White addressed speculation about their relationship Monday, following an animated sideline discussion during Saturday's 100-84 loss to Portland. Both dismissed concerns, characterizing the exchange as routine coaching.

The on-court interaction had drawn observer attention, but Clark and White's public statements affirmed their relationship remains solid. They described the discussion as a normal part of the game and coaching process.

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk advances to French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian player upset fellow countrywoman Elina Svitolina and will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in the next round.
cards.body:
Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk defeated fellow countryman Elina Svitolina in a French Open quarterfinal match, securing her place in the semifinals. Following the victory, Kostyuk dedicated her win to Ukraine.

She will next face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva, who advanced to the semifinals after a dominant performance against Sorana Cirstea. The matchup sets up a compelling semifinal clash between the Ukrainian player and the rising Russian star.

hero.headline: Tom Holland Delayed Spider-Man Film to Star in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey
hero.body:
Tom Holland called Sony Pictures boss Tom Rothman to request delaying production on Spider-Man: Brand New Day so he could film Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, the actor revealed in GQ magazine's summer cover story. Holland described the conversation as uncomfortable and said the request was a tough pill to swallow at first.

Nolan offered Holland a role in his epic film, creating a scheduling conflict with the next Spider-Man installment. The actor chose to prioritize the Nolan project, requiring him to push back the start of production on the superhero franchise that has defined much of his career. Holland has played Spider-Man in multiple films for Sony and Marvel Studios since his debut in the role in 2016.

The decision represents a significant choice for Holland, who has become one of Hollywood's most recognizable actors largely through his portrayal of Peter Parker. Taking a role in a Nolan film carries major prestige in the industry, as the director is known for ambitious, critically acclaimed projects. The Odyssey marks Nolan's adaptation of the ancient Greek epic poem.

Sony's willingness to adjust the production schedule indicates the studio's continued investment in Holland as Spider-Man. The delay affects the timeline for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, though no specific dates for either film's production were disclosed in the interview. Holland's frank acknowledgment of the difficult conversation with Rothman offers a rare glimpse into the business negotiations that occur behind major casting decisions.

The scheduling conflict highlights the competing demands faced by actors who anchor major franchises while pursuing other career opportunities. Holland's choice to film The Odyssey first suggests he views the Nolan project as a critical opportunity for his development as an actor beyond the superhero genre.

cards.headline: BET Forms First Advisory Board With Queen Latifah, LL Cool J, and Founder Bob Johnson
cards.teaser: The network named six members to guide its evolution at the intersection of media, community, and culture.
cards.body:
Paramount Skydance's BET has created its first board of advisers, announcing that six cultural icons, business leaders, and industry visionaries will help guide the brand's continued evolution. The inaugural board includes BET founder Bob Johnson, Queen Latifah, and LL Cool J among its six members.

The network described the advisory board as a group that will help shape BET's direction as a force at the intersection of media, community, and culture. This marks the first time in the network's history that it has established such a formal advisory structure.

cards.headline: Tribeca Festival Defends Premiere of AI-Generated Film About Iran Protests
cards.teaser: Co-founder Jane Rosenthal said Dreams of Violets about Iranian civilian resistance should be seen right now at this time.
cards.body:
Tribeca Film Festival co-founder Jane Rosenthal defended the festival's decision to premiere Dreams of Violets, a fully AI-generated film about the Iranian civilian resistance. Speaking at the festival's 25th anniversary cocktail reception in lower Manhattan, Rosenthal said people need to read director Ash Koosha's statement about the film.

Koosha is Iranian, and Rosenthal told Variety that the film should be seen right now at this time. The premiere represents a significant moment for AI-generated cinema at a major film festival, with Rosenthal standing by the programming choice despite questions about the use of artificial intelligence in filmmaking.

cards.headline: Netflix UK Unscripted Chief Warns Against AI Use in Reality Shows
cards.teaser: Syeda Irtizaali said it's hard now to tell what is fake and what is real.
cards.body:
Syeda Irtizaali, Netflix's UK director of unscripted content, expressed concerns about incorporating AI into reality television during remarks at SXSW London. She cited difficulties in distinguishing authentic content from artificially generated material as a key reason for her reluctance.

While Irtizaali acknowledged Netflix's tech-forward approach and described AI as a useful development tool for creative ideation, she drew a clear line between using the technology during production planning and integrating it into final reality show outputs.

cards.headline: Permut Presentations Acquires Rights to JJ Velazquez Story for Film
cards.teaser: The company plans a narrative feature about the Sing Sing star who served nearly 24 years for a murder he did not commit.
cards.body:
Permut Presentations has secured the life rights of Jon-Adrian "JJ" Velazquez, who spent nearly 24 years in prison for a murder conviction he did not commit. The company has also acquired reporting rights from NBC News journalist Dan Slepian, a senior producer at Dateline who covered Velazquez's case.

The planned narrative feature will chronicle the relationship between Velazquez and Slepian throughout his legal fight to overturn his conviction. Velazquez is known for his appearance in the film Sing Sing.

cards.headline: Will Arnett Joins Kristen Stewart in Amazon's The Challenger Series
cards.teaser: Arnett will play NASA official George Abbey in the limited series about astronaut Sally Ride and the Challenger disaster.
cards.body:
Will Arnett will star opposite Kristen Stewart in the upcoming Amazon Prime Video limited series about NASA astronaut Sally Ride and the Challenger shuttle disaster. Arnett will play NASA official George Abbey in the show.

Amazon officially picked up the series in March with Stewart attached to play Ride. The series is inspired by Meredith E. Bagby's book The New Guys.

cards.headline: Black Crowes Frontman Clashes With Florida Crowd Over USA Chant
cards.teaser: Chris Robinson told the audience he did not know what they had to be so proud of right now.
cards.body:
Black Crowes frontman Chris Robinson stirred controversy at a Florida concert when he rejected a patriotic chant from the audience. After fans began chanting "U.S.A.," Robinson pushed back, questioning what they had to be proud of in the current moment. His remarks drew a mixed reaction—some booed while others cheered his response.

Robinson's challenge to the crowd reflected broader tensions around expressions of nationalism at live events. The exchange highlighted the divide between those embracing patriotic sentiment and those questioning the country's current direction.

hero.headline: Marco Rubio and Todd Blanche to testify before House
hero.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche will appear before the House for testimony on Tuesday morning.
hero.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche are scheduled to testify before the House on Tuesday morning. The hearing follows the announcement that Bill Pulte will replace Tulsi Gabbard as Director of National Intelligence.

The testimony comes as the administration manages foreign policy challenges including ongoing issues with Iran and Taiwan. Both officials are expected to face questions about administration priorities and recent policy decisions.

cards.headline: Trump reportedly confronted Netanyahu over Hezbollah attack plans
cards.teaser: President Trump criticized Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a phone call over plans to escalate military action in Lebanon.
cards.body:
President Trump angrily confronted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the phone Monday, objecting to Israel's plans to resume airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs. According to reports, Trump used profanity during the heated call, demanding to know what Netanyahu was doing. The confrontation came after Iran announced it would suspend talks with the US in response to Israel's military campaign in Lebanon.

Democratic strategist David Axelrod defended Trump's response, saying his analysis of the situation was justified. The clash underscores ongoing disagreements between the two leaders over Israel's military strategy and the risks it poses to regional stability.

cards.headline: Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass faces primary challenge from TV star and council member
cards.teaser: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass is competing in a tight primary race against city council member Nithya Raman and reality TV personality Spencer Pratt.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass is seeking reelection in a primary race against two challengers. City council member Nithya Raman, a former ally, and Spencer Pratt, known from reality television, are competing for the position.

Primary results were being tabulated Tuesday as voters decided whether to grant Bass another term or advance one of her challengers to a runoff. The race has drawn attention due to the diverse backgrounds of the candidates and the challenges facing the city.

cards.headline: California governor primary narrows field to replace Gavin Newsom
cards.teaser: Democrats Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra compete against Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton in the race to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
California voters are selecting candidates in the primary race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Three Democrats are competing for their party's nomination: Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra. On the Republican side, Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton are seeking their party's nod.

California uses an open primary system, known as the "jungle primary," that has been in place since 2012. Under this system, voters can select any candidate regardless of party registration. The setup was designed to increase competition in races that Democrats had dominated for years.

cards.headline: New Mexico lawmakers issue subpoenas in Jeffrey Epstein ranch investigation
cards.teaser: A bipartisan special committee investigating Jeffrey Epstein's Zorro Ranch will send subpoenas to 14 entities including government agencies.
cards.body:
A bipartisan special committee of New Mexico lawmakers announced Monday that it will issue its first round of subpoenas in its investigation of Jeffrey Epstein's Zorro Ranch near Santa Fe. The New Mexico Truth Commission, created specifically to examine Epstein's activities in the state, will send subpoenas to 14 entities.

The recipients include agencies that previously investigated Epstein. The committee's work aims to uncover details about his operations at the remote New Mexico property and examine whether authorities adequately responded to earlier information about his activities.

cards.headline: New Mexico governor primary features former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland
cards.teaser: Five candidates including former Biden administration official Deb Haaland are competing to replace Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham.
cards.body:
New Mexico voters are selecting gubernatorial candidates in a primary featuring former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland. She faces Sam Bregman, Gregg Hull, Duke Rodriguez, and Doug Turner in the race to succeed Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham.

Haaland served in the Biden administration before entering the race. The contest will determine which candidates advance to the general election to lead the state.

cards.headline: Trump signs executive order on artificial intelligence
cards.teaser: President Trump signed a revised executive order
